summary: A browser page for your Calibre library: read, search and send books to an e-reader.
does: Calibre-Web gives your Calibre book library its own page on your home network. From a browser you can read books, search the library and send books to an e-reader.

It reads your books folder and never changes it, so uploading or editing books in Calibre-Web does not work. You add and change books with Calibre itself. Starboard chooses the port, 8083 when it is free, and shows the address with an Open button.
for: People who keep their books in a Calibre library and want to read, search and send them to an e-reader from any browser at home.
needs: A Calibre library in the books folder of your media folder, a folder containing metadata.db. Nothing else beyond Starboard with plug-in API 1.14 or later. Change Calibre-Web's first sign-in password at once, as anyone on your home network can open the page.
shows: No dashboard card and no settings in Starboard. Its tab in Settings, Plug-ins has an Open Calibre-Web button, and Activate, Deactivate and Remove buttons. Everything else is set in Calibre-Web's own page, where you give it the location of your Calibre database.
unclear: Is it correct to name the first sign-in details in public text, or should the storefront only say to change the password at once?
